title: Number Quest Unit 7 · The Test Range (Pro)

items.q: Seven probes landed at 9, 12, 15, 10, 15, 18 and 11 meters. What is the median landing?
misconceptions: took the middle of the list as written, without putting it in order
correct
took the middle of the range, halfway from 9 to 18
chose the landing that appears most often
items.why: Put the landings in order: 9, 10, 11, 12, 15, 15, 18. The middle one of the seven is the 4th, so the median is 12 meters.

items.q: A box plot of landings shows: lowest 5, lower quartile 9, median 12, upper quartile 16, highest 21 (meters). What is the interquartile range?
misconceptions: gave the range, from the lowest to the highest
subtracted the median from the upper quartile
gave the median, a center and not a spread
correct
items.why: The interquartile range is the width of the box: upper quartile minus lower quartile. 16 − 9 = 7 meters.

items.q: Launcher A's landings have a median of 14 m and an interquartile range of 2 m. Launcher B's have a median of 14 m and an interquartile range of 8 m. Which is true?
choices: B's landings vary more than A's
B's probes land farther than A's
A and B land in exactly the same places
A's landings vary more than B's
misconceptions: correct
thought a bigger spread means longer landings
thought the same median means the same data
read the smaller interquartile range as more spread
items.why: The median is a center and the interquartile range is a spread. Both medians are 14, but B's middle half is 8 m wide and A's only 2 m, so B's landings vary more.

items.q: Which probability means that an event is unlikely?
misconceptions: chose 0.5, which is as likely as not
correct
thought a bigger number means less likely
chose a number bigger than 1, which no probability can be
items.why: A probability is a number from 0 to 1. Near 0 is unlikely, 0.5 is as likely as not, and near 1 is likely. So 0.15 is unlikely. Nothing has a probability above 1.

items.q: A probe was dropped 80 times and landed in bin D 24 times. About how many times would you expect bin D in 400 drops?
misconceptions: kept the count from the 80 drops
assumed four bins are equally likely and divided 400 by 4
correct
added the 320 extra drops to the count
items.why: The relative frequency is 24 ÷ 80 = 0.3. At the same rate, 0.3 × 400 = 120 drops would land in bin D.

items.q: A drop tower has 8 equal bins: 3 red, 4 blue and 1 green. A probe is equally likely to land in each bin. What is the probability it lands in a blue bin?
misconceptions: thought the three colors are equally likely
gave the number of blue bins, not a probability
correct
put 1 over the number of blue bins
items.why: Each of the 8 bins is equally likely, and 4 of them are blue. The probability is 4/8 = 1/2.

items.q: Launcher A: mean 18 m, mean absolute deviation 3 m. Launcher B: mean 27 m, mean absolute deviation 3 m. How many of those deviations apart are the means?
misconceptions: correct
gave the gap in meters, not in deviations
compared the two deviations, which are equal, instead of the means
subtracted the deviation once from the gap
items.why: The means are 27 − 18 = 9 meters apart. Each deviation is 3 meters, and 9 ÷ 3 = 3. The means are 3 deviations apart.

items.q: In a scatter plot of launches, as the launch power goes up, the distance goes down for most launches. What does the plot show?
misconceptions: thought any clear pattern is a positive one
correct
thought an association needs the points to go up
named one odd point instead of the pattern
items.why: When one quantity goes up as the other goes down, the points fall from left to right. That is a negative association.

items.q: The points of a scatter plot are (1, 5), (2, 8), (3, 11), (4, 2), (5, 17) and (6, 20). Which point is an outlier?
misconceptions: chose the point with the largest values
chose the point with the smallest values
chose the point that comes right after the odd one
correct
items.why: The other points go up by 3 each time: 5, 8, 11, then 14, 17, 20. At 4 the pattern gives 14, but the point is at 2, far below. So (4, 2) is the outlier.
